subject: ss-haematology
title: Chronic myeloid leukaemia: BCR-ABL1 phases and TKI milestones
refs: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, CML chapter

steps.tx: **Chronic myeloid leukaemia** (CML) arises from a **pluripotent haematopoietic stem cell**. A reciprocal **t(9;22)(q34;q11)** translocation, the **Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome**, fuses **BCR** on chromosome 22 with **ABL1** from chromosome 9 to form **BCR-ABL1**. The fusion encodes a **constitutively active tyrosine kinase** (TK) that the leukaemic clone depends on, a state called **oncogene addiction**.
steps.say: Every case carries this one rearranged chromosome, so the disease has a single, known driver. The fusion protein stays switched on and sits in the cytoplasm, while normal ABL1 is tightly controlled and lives in the nucleus. That constant signal is exactly what a targeted tablet can block.

rows: Mostly Ph-positive acute lymphoblastic leukaemia; kinase activity higher than p210
Rare, very slow CML; kinase activity lower than p210

steps.tx: CML makes up **15%** to **20%** of adult leukaemias, with an incidence of **0.6** to **2** per **100,000** per year, and it is less frequent in children. The **male-to-female ratio** is **1.3** to **1.8**, and incidence peaks at **64** to **68** years in the Western world. Most patients (**90%** to **95%**) are diagnosed in **chronic phase**, and **50%** of patients in the United States have no symptoms at diagnosis.
steps.say: Many patients are found on a routine blood count and feel well. When symptoms appear they are tiredness, weight loss and discomfort from an enlarged spleen. Advanced disease adds bone pain, night sweats, infections, bleeding and symptoms of leukostasis.

steps.tx: The hallmark of new CML is **hyperleukocytosis** with a marked **left shift**, including **basophilia** and **eosinophilia**. WBC can exceed **450,000/µL**, and the **G:E index** (granulopoiesis to erythropoiesis) in marrow is often above **3:1**. Raised **lactate dehydrogenase** and **uric acid** reflect hyperproliferation, while platelets may be high or low.
steps.say: Reactive leukocytosis rarely goes above 50 × 10⁹/L and has no basophilia. Other myeloproliferative neoplasms lack the BCR-ABL1 fusion, and atypical CML has no Ph chromosome, so the molecular test is what separates them. Treatment is usually not an emergency even at very high counts.

rows: WBC usually rarely above 50 × 10⁹/L; toxic granulation; no basophilia or peripheral myeloblasts; no BCR-ABL1
No BCR-ABL1; mutant JAK2, CALR or MPL usually found
No Ph chromosome or BCR-ABL1 rearrangement; SETBP1 or ETNK1 mutation in about 40%; no basophilia; median survival 2 to 3 years

steps.tx: Three **phases** decide prognosis: **chronic phase (CP)**, **accelerated phase (AP)** and **blast crisis (BC)**. **AP** is blasts **15%** to **29%** in blood or marrow, blasts plus promyelocytes above **30%** with blasts below **30%**, basophils **20%** or more, or **persistent thrombocytopenia** below **100 × 10⁹/L** unrelated to therapy. **BC** needs blasts above **30%** or extramedullary blast proliferation excluding the spleen.
steps.say: Phase drives the whole plan. Chronic phase responds best to TKIs. Accelerated phase still has real chances of durable response, only slightly lower than chronic phase. Blast crisis acts like acute leukaemia with a poor outlook, and the 30 percent blast line is the number to remember.

rows: Patients who meet neither AP nor BC criteria
Most patients are diagnosed here; TKI monotherapy; best response
Blasts 15% to 29%; or blasts plus promyelocytes above 30% with blasts below 30%; basophils 20% or more; persistent thrombocytopenia below 100 × 10⁹/L
Durable response still possible; allogeneic transplant to be considered; long-term TKI an option when blasts are not increased; 4-year PFS 49% and OS 59% with bosutinib in one phase II study
Blasts above 30% or extramedullary blast proliferation excluding the spleen
Expected survival under 1 year; restore haematologic response with TKI or intensive chemotherapy, then allogeneic transplant, the only option with long-term survival

steps.tx: Diagnosis needs a demonstrated **BCR-ABL1** fusion, shown by **karyotype** with the Ph chromosome in at least **20** bone marrow metaphases (typical t(9;22) in **80%** to **90%**) or by **PCR** for the transcript. **FISH** (fluorescence in situ hybridisation) is used for masked or variant translocations, and a multiplex PCR is mandatory when splenomegaly and high WBC exist without a visible Ph chromosome. Baseline risk is graded by scores such as **Sokal**.
steps.say: Cytogenetics needs dividing marrow cells, which is why a marrow aspirate is part of the workup. Scores grade risk before treatment starts. The molecular PCR tests are what track response afterwards.

nodes.label: Karyotype: Ph in at least 20 metaphases
Multiplex PCR if no Ph seen
FISH for masked or variant translocation
BCR-ABL1 confirmed; phase and risk set

steps.tx: Four **TKIs** are approved for first-line chronic phase CML: **imatinib**, **dasatinib**, **nilotinib** and **bosutinib**. Treatment starts as soon as the diagnosis is confirmed, and **hydroxyurea** is needed only if the patient is symptomatic or diagnostics take longer than **3** to **5** days. **Allopurinol** (**100** to **300** mg per day) controls hyperuricaemia until a complete haematologic response.
steps.say: Imatinib is the reference drug, and most data come from it. Tumour lysis is rarely seen with TKIs, so generous fluid intake is the main precaution. Symptoms usually fade within one to two weeks.

rows: FDA approval 2001; first-line standard from the IRIS trial

steps.tx: The **IRIS** trial randomised **1,106** chronic phase patients to imatinib or interferon, and imatinib gave significantly higher haematologic and major cytogenetic response rates. Fifteen controlled first-line studies found second-generation TKIs gave **faster** and **deeper** falls in BCR-ABL1 transcripts, but no study showed a difference in progression-free or overall survival. Second-generation drugs carry **more serious** adverse events, especially cardiovascular ones, so the choice weighs response speed against toxicity.
steps.say: Imatinib set the standard every newer drug had to match. Second-generation drugs buy speed and depth at the price of more serious side effects. Stems often name the toxicity and expect you to name the drug, so learn the signature harm of each one.

Pleural and pericardial effusions in 30% to 40%
Pulmonary hypertension in under 5%; lymphocytosis up to 73%; flu-like syndrome eased by paracetamol 1 g for 5 to 7 days

steps.tx: Response is measured at **three levels**. A **complete haematologic response** (CHR) needs normal blood counts, no symptoms and normal spleen size. A **complete cytogenetic response** (CCyR) means no **Ph-positive** metaphase in at least **20** evaluated, while a **partial** response shows **1%** to **35%** Ph-positive metaphases. **Molecular response** is read by quantitative PCR on the International Scale (IS), and **major molecular response** (MMR) is a BCR-ABL1 ratio below **0.1%**.
steps.say: Haematologic response only shows that proliferation has slowed, and hydroxyurea can also achieve it. A cytogenetic response means normal marrow is regrowing, and it predicts long-term control. Molecular PCR is the most sensitive level, reaching about one leukaemic cell in 100,000.

rows: Normal counts, symptoms gone, spleen normal
Proliferation slowed; hydroxyurea can achieve it
Normal marrow; strongest predictor of survival
No BCR-ABL1 amplification; written CMR/4, CMR/4.5, CMR/5 by control gene level
Used when cytogenetics is already documented

steps.tx: Three **milestones** must not be missed: **CHR by 1 month**, **Ph-negative haematopoiesis** at least in part by **3 or 6 months**, and **CCyR by 12 months**. QPCR should fall steadily and may reach below **10%** by the **3rd** or **6th** month. If CCyR is lost or QPCR rises by at least **0.5 log**, check adherence first, then study the residual cells, and repeat cytogenetics every **3** months until CCyR.
steps.say: Milestones are checkpoints, not verdicts. The first step when a checkpoint is missed is always a careful adherence check with the patient and family. Only after that does a mutation screen earn its place.

rows: CHR, reached in over 80% of patients within 4 weeks
Ph-negative haematopoiesis at least in part; QPCR possibly below 10% by 3rd or 6th month
CCyR, reached in 65% to 85% of patients within 12 months
Mutation screen; FISH for BCR-ABL1 amplification

steps.tx: Mutation screening after at least **3** months of treatment finds a mutation in **30%** to **40%** of failures; repeat it after **1** to **2** months if there is still no response. The **T315I** gatekeeper mutation resists all TKIs except **ponatinib** in the mutation data, and **asciminib** binds the **myristoyl pocket** and shows activity against T315I. **BCR-ABL1 amplification** causes resistance in **10%** to **15%** of cases and responds to a dose increase.
steps.say: The mutation map tells you which drug to drop, not which drug will work. A clone can carry extra mutations outside the kinase domain that defeat even a well-matched drug. Slow deterioration is often rescued by an imatinib dose increase before any switch.

rows: Impairs imatinib and all second-generation TKIs; all TKIs except ponatinib inactive in the mutation data
Inhibits all known BCR-ABL1 mutations including T315I; approved 2012; initial dose 45 mg daily
Binds the myristoyl pocket; FDA approved October 2021 for T315I or after two or more TKIs
Protein synthesis inhibitor active against T315I; FDA approved October 2012 after failure of two or more TKIs
New response in more than 80% when response was lost slowly

steps.tx: Stopping a TKI is a trial, not a cure. In the STIM trial, patients on imatinib in **continuous complete molecular remission (CMR) for at least 2 years** were enrolled, and about **50%** relapsed, most within the first **7** to **8** months, with late relapses up to **48** months. Remission is more likely after treatment longer than **5** years, CMR longer than **2** years, a negative digital PCR before stopping, and older age.
steps.say: TKIs do not kill leukaemic stem cells, so almost every patient keeps residual disease, and even deep responders can relapse. Patients who stop need close molecular checks, monthly or every other month for the first 8 months. Relapse is treated by restarting the drug.

rows: Continuous CMR for at least 2 years; MR4 or higher has a similar chance of staying in remission as CMR
About 50%; most within 7 to 8 months; late relapse up to 48 months
After a new CMR, about 30% stay in remission
Treatment over 5 years; CMR over 2 years; negative digital PCR; older age
Monthly or bimonthly for the first 8 months; every 3 to 4 months for 4 years; then once or twice a year indefinitely
Every 3 to 4 months in the first 5 years, then every 6 to 12 months; continue indefinitely, as relapse is documented beyond 20 years from diagnosis
BCR-ABL1 positive cells persist in almost all patients who stop, including those who do not restart

steps.tx: High-yield for the exam: the genetics is **t(9;22)** making **BCR-ABL1**, and **AP** is **15%** to **29%** blasts while **BC** is above **30%** blasts. First-line doses are **imatinib 400 mg** daily, **dasatinib 100 mg** daily, **nilotinib 300 mg** twice daily fasting and **bosutinib 400 mg**, with **T315I** needing **ponatinib** or **asciminib**. Milestones are **CHR by 1 month**, **CCyR by 12 months**, **MMR** below **0.1%** on the IS, **MR4.5** below **1/32,000**, and mutation screening after **3** months finds **30%** to **40%**. Pleural effusion marks **dasatinib**, metabolic and arterial harm marks **nilotinib**, and arterial and venous events mark **ponatinib**; stopping needs **CMR** for at least **2** years and about **50%** relapse.
steps.say: Memorise the numbers as a set. The blast percentages set the phase, the dose list is the first-line choice, and the mutation map tells you which drug to drop. Remember that MMR is the 0.1 percent line, and that MR4.5 is a much deeper ratio.

rows: CHR by 1 month; CCyR by 12 months
CMR for at least 2 years; about 50% relapse
